html:
SMTO-FIL-0027 — SMTO lost its place while reading a file in parts

GUID: e43f590f-0597-4d80-977a-c297c8084ec1
Slug: file-stale-cursor
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO was reading a long file or folder list in parts, but its bookmark for the next part expired, the Gateway restarted, or the file changed. Nothing was changed; the read just needs to start over.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to read that file or folder again from the beginning. A fresh read gives SMTO a new, valid bookmark for the following parts.
  2. If the file is still being written, such as a growing log, wait until it stops changing, or ask SMTO to read only the newest lines. Each change to the file cancels the old bookmark, so a moving file keeps breaking the read.
  3. If more than an hour has passed since SMTO started reading, or the Gateway was restarted, ask SMTO to start the read over when you continue. Bookmarks last at most an hour and are cleared whenever the Gateway restarts.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads the whole file or list without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to continue from its old place; that bookmark will be refused again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file read, list or search continuation cursor was rejected because it is unknown, expired (one hour) or evicted, was issued by an earlier Gateway provider generation or for another root or namespace, or the file's revision changed since the previous chunk.

What this means

  • The cursor is absent, expired, from another Gateway generation, malformed after decoding, or no longer matches the file's current revision/type/existence. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The cursor is absent, expired, from another Gateway generation, malformed after decoding, or no longer matches the file's current revision/type/existence.

How to diagnose it

  • Check cursor age/generation and current file state; reusing a changed-file offset can skip or duplicate content.

How to fix it

  • Discard the cursor and restart the read, list or search without one, then continue only with cursors from the new responses; for files that are still changing, read with tail_lines or wait until writes stop (gateway_core/file_common.CursorStore.read, Operation.uncursor, file_read.read).
  • Restart the bounded read, listing or search from current state and use only its newly returned cursor.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh initial read/list/search returns a current cursor and consistent continuation.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors
